the production of novel activated carbons from LC precursors, which have shown a significant potential for phenol adsorption.
the production of activated carbons from renewable LC sources.
the development of new adsorbents for the phenol removal from water.

the adsorption of phenolic compounds onto the novel AC is governed by the surface properties, which in turn are influenced by the precursor, the activation process and the pH of the solution.

the adsorption of phenols on the novel activated carbons produced from rapeseed and from kenaf is a complex process that depends on the nature of the adsorbent surface, the concentration, and pH of the solution.

the adsorption of phenols onto activated carbons produced from lignocelulosic materials is a feasible process to treat phenol-containing wastewaters.
